decisions.reason: As a recently launched carpet that fits the firm's broad interior-accessories offer and was given its own product page, it is more likely to be retained unless early demand proved clearly weak.
The hand-knotted wool silk carpet matches the firm's craftsmanship-led positioning and premium material expertise, so management would usually keep it on the market beyond its first year.
Although another low-pile decorative carpet faces some overlap risk within a broad assortment, its close fit with the existing range and fresh launch still favor continuation.
A corner bench builds directly on the firm's core furniture business for residential and project interiors, making withdrawal within a year relatively unlikely.
This low-pile carpet is close to the established accessories offer and still newly introduced, so management would usually keep it unless assortment simplification became necessary.
A swivel shell chair fits well with the firm's residential, workplace and public-interior focus, and a new seating product would normally be given more time in a growing market.
